name: RMS Titanic
summary: The 'unsinkable' liner that sank on its maiden voyage after striking an iceberg; ~1,500 died.
story: Struck an iceberg on 14 April 1912 and sank in under three hours; too few lifeboats led to new safety rules (SOLAS 1914).
discovery: Found by Robert Ballard and Jean-Louis Michel in 1985 using the towed camera sled Argo; a full 3D scan was made in 2022–23.
science: Iron-eating bacteria (Halomonas titanicae) form 'rusticles' that are slowly consuming the hull.

name: Endurance
summary: Shackleton's ship, crushed by sea ice; all 28 men survived after an epic escape.
story: Trapped in Weddell Sea ice in 1915 and crushed; Shackleton sailed 1,300 km in an open boat to South Georgia to get help.
discovery: Found in 2022 by the Endurance22 expedition with Sabertooth underwater robots, remarkably intact.
science: No wood-boring shipworms in Antarctic waters, so the wood is preserved.

name: HMS Erebus
summary: Flagship of the lost Franklin expedition searching for the Northwest Passage.
story: Both ships were abandoned in ice; all 129 men died.
discovery: Found in 2014 by Parks Canada guided by Inuit oral history; HMS Terror was found in 2016.
science: Shows how Indigenous knowledge solved a 170-year mystery.

name: HMS Terror
summary: Franklin's second ship, found almost intact in 2016.
story: Abandoned with Erebus in 1848.
discovery: Located after a tip from an Inuk crew member.

name: Vasa
summary: A Swedish warship that capsized on its maiden voyage, raised almost intact in 1961.
story: Top-heavy design; it sank less than 1.5 km into its first trip.
discovery: Found by Anders Franzén in 1956; now in Stockholm's Vasa Museum.
science: The Baltic's low salinity excludes shipworms.

name: Mary Rose
summary: Henry VIII's flagship that sank in battle against the French.
story: Heeled over and flooded through open gunports.
discovery: Raised in 1982; its preserved half-hull is in Portsmouth.

name: Antikythera wreck
summary: Contained the Antikythera mechanism, an ancient Greek astronomical computer.
story: Sank around 60 BCE carrying luxury goods.
discovery: Found by sponge divers in 1900.
science: The mechanism predicted eclipses with bronze gears.

name: Uluburun shipwreck
summary: A 3,300-year-old ship carrying copper, tin, glass and gold from many cultures.
story: Late Bronze Age trading vessel.
discovery: Found by a sponge diver in 1982; excavated 1984–94.
science: Evidence of Bronze Age global trade.

name: Black Sea MAP Greek ship
summary: The oldest intact shipwreck known, ~2,400 years old.
story: A trading vessel lost in deep water.
discovery: Found by the Black Sea Maritime Archaeology Project with ROVs.

name: San José galleon
summary: The 'holy grail of shipwrecks', possibly carrying billions in gold and silver.
story: Sunk by the British in the War of the Spanish Succession.
discovery: Found by Colombia with REMUS AUVs in 2015.
science: Ownership disputed between Colombia, Spain and Indigenous groups.

name: Bismarck
summary: Germany's mighty battleship sunk after a chase across the Atlantic.
story: Sunk by the Royal Navy three days after sinking HMS Hood.
discovery: Found by Robert Ballard in 1989.

name: USS Indianapolis
summary: Torpedoed after delivering atomic bomb parts; many survivors died from sharks and exposure.
story: Sank in 12 minutes; ~316 of 1,195 survived.
discovery: Found by Paul Allen's RV Petrel in 2017.
science: Shark attacks on survivors were among the worst recorded.

name: USS Johnston
summary: The deepest shipwreck ever surveyed by crewed submersible (2021).
story: Sunk in the Battle off Samar.
discovery: Surveyed by Victor Vescovo in Limiting Factor.

name: Yamato
summary: The largest battleship ever built, sunk by US aircraft.
story: Sunk on a one-way mission to Okinawa.
discovery: Located in 1985.

name: Lusitania
summary: Torpedoed by a German U-boat, helping bring the US into WWI.
story: Sank in 18 minutes; 1,198 died.
discovery: Located in 1935.

name: SS Thistlegorm
summary: A famous dive site filled with WWII motorbikes, trucks and trains.
story: Bombed by German aircraft.
discovery: Found by Jacques Cousteau.

name: Truk Lagoon fleet
summary: Over 50 ships sunk in Operation Hailstone, now a reef-covered underwater museum.
story: US air raid on the Japanese base.
discovery: Explored by Cousteau's team in 1969.
science: Leaking fuel is a pollution risk.

name: Batavia
summary: Wrecked off Australia, followed by a notorious mutiny and massacre.
story: Ran aground on a reef.
discovery: Located in 1963; hull in Fremantle.
science: Early contact between Europeans and Australia.

name: Edmund Fitzgerald
summary: The largest ship lost on the Great Lakes, in a November storm.
story: Sank with all 29 crew.
discovery: Found days later by aircraft magnetometer.

name: Belitung shipwreck
summary: A 9th-century Arab ship carrying ~60,000 Chinese ceramics.
story: Evidence of the maritime Silk Road.
discovery: Found by sea-cucumber divers.

name: Dwarka submerged ruins
summary: Offshore stone structures off Dwarka linked by some to the legendary city.
story: Ancient coastal settlement remains.
discovery: Surveyed by the National Institute of Oceanography (S.R. Rao) from 1983.

name: Mahabalipuram submerged temples
summary: Structures revealed after the 2004 tsunami shifted sand.
story: Possibly linked to the legend of the Seven Pagodas.
discovery: Surveyed by NIO and the Scientific Exploration Society in 2002 and after 2004.

name: SS Tilawa
summary: The 'Indian Titanic': torpedoed with ~958 people aboard, many Indian passengers.
story: Sunk by a Japanese submarine; 280 died.
discovery: Located in 2017 by salvors recovering its silver.

name: Andrea Doria
summary: Italian liner sunk after a collision; the 'Mount Everest of wreck diving'.
story: Collided with MS Stockholm in fog.
discovery: Sank the next day; 46 died.

name: HMHS Britannic
summary: Titanic's sister ship, sunk by a mine in WWI.
story: Sank in 55 minutes; 30 died.
discovery: Found by Cousteau in 1975.

name: Whydah Gally
summary: The only authenticated pirate shipwreck, captained by 'Black Sam' Bellamy.
story: Wrecked in a storm.
discovery: Found by Barry Clifford in 1984.

name: Kronan
summary: A Swedish flagship that exploded in battle.
story: Capsized and its magazine exploded.
discovery: Found in 1980.

name: Mars
summary: A 16th-century Swedish flagship, among the best-preserved of its age.
story: Sank in battle.
discovery: Found in 2011.

name: SS Central America
summary: The 'Ship of Gold' whose loss helped trigger the Panic of 1857.
story: Sank in a hurricane carrying California gold.
discovery: Found using sonar and statistical search theory (Bayesian search).

name: Malaysia Airlines MH370 search
summary: The largest underwater search ever, which mapped ~120,000 km² of unknown seafloor.
story: Aircraft disappeared on 8 March 2014.
discovery: Not found; renewed searches in 2018 and 2025.
science: The search revealed new seafloor features in great detail.
